details.description: Base General is the default model in Deepgram's Base tier of speech-to-text models, tuned for everyday audio processing rather than a specific domain. Deepgram's Models & Languages Overview lists Base, together with Enhanced and Nova 1, under "Legacy Models." Unlike the domain-specific Base variants (meeting, phonecall, finance, video), which are English only, Base General supports about twenty languages. It is built on Deepgram's end-to-end deep learning speech recognition architecture.
advantages: Is the default Base-tier model, documented as "(Default) Optimized for everyday audio processing."

Supports about twenty languages, including Chinese, Dutch, French, German, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Swedish and Turkish, unlike the domain-specific Base variants, which are English only.

Deepgram describes Base-tier models as built on its "signature end-to-end deep learning speech-to-text model architecture," offering "a solid combination of accuracy and cost effectiveness in some cases."
disadvantages: Deepgram lists the Base tier under "Legacy Models" in its Models & Languages Overview.
Deepgram states its Enhanced-tier "general" model is "likely to be more accurate than any region-specific Base model for the language for which it is enabled."
Deepgram states its Enhanced-tier models "generally have higher accuracy and better word recognition" than Base models and "handle uncommon words significantly better."
use_cases: General-purpose transcription of everyday audio across the model's supported languages.

notes: No word-error-rate or other accuracy figures specific to base-general were found on Deepgram's maker pages, so evaluations is left empty. Languages are as listed in Deepgram's Models & Languages Overview table for `base`/`base-general` (Deepgram lists Dutch and Flemish under the same code `nl`). Legacy status: developers.deepgram.com/docs/model does not use the word, but developers.deepgram.com/docs/models-languages-overview groups Nova (1), Enhanced and Base under a 'Legacy Models' heading. The catalog carries no deprecation_date.
